bihar_raw_news.title: Drip Capital partners with Bihar government to provide Rs 5000 crore trade finance for ...
bihar_raw_news.content: Pushkar Mukewar, Founder and CEO, Drip Capital, and Aman Samir Director of MSME for the Government of Bihar. Drip Capital, a tech-enabled trade finance platform, has signed a Memorandum of Understanding (MoU) with the Department of Industries, Government of Bihar, on the sidelines of an investor meet organised jointly by the central and state governments in Patna. Under this partnership, Drip Capital has pledged to facilitate up to Rs 5,000 crore in trade finance over five years to support MSME exporters in Bihar and strengthen their access to international markets . The collateral-free finance will cover MSME working capital needs, with funding available in as little as 24-48 hours. Drip Capital's digital underwriting means small units with no banking history or assets can access formal credit based on their trade. Further, Drip Capital will leverage its B2B cross-border trade platform to connect Bihar's manufacturers with overseas buyers, enabling them to explore new export opportunities and expand their presence in global markets. This will start with a trade marketplace in Darbhanga and Madhubani, giving sellers of makhana, Madhubani textiles, and handicrafts direct access to verified domestic and international buyers, with early payment to sellers. The MoU was signed by Pushkar Mukewar, Founder and CEO, Drip Capital, in the presence of the Chief Minister of Bihar, Samrat Chaudhary; Shreyasi Singh Minister of Industries; Lav Agrawal, Director General Foreign Trade; Kundan Kumar (IAS) Secretary Department of Industries; and Aman Samir (IAS), Director of MSME, along with other senior state government officials. Pushkar Mukewar, Founder and CEO, Drip Capital, said, in a statement, "Bihar has significant potential to emerge as an important contributor to India's export economy, given its diverse manufacturing base, traditional industries and entrepreneurial ecosystem. However, enabling businesses to participate in global trade requires more than access to international buyers. It also requires timely financing, market linkages and the right institutional support. Through this partnership, we aim to bring these elements together and help local businesses become more competitive in international markets." Live Events As part of the MoU, Drip Capital will also collaborate with the Bihar Khadi Board and JEEViKA to support local producers and enterprises in accessing export opportunities, linking 100 producer groups and FPOs. Drip Capital will also finance buyers of artisan and self-help group products, so producers are paid on time when they sell through aggregators and exporters. The partnership will include initiatives around Special Economic Zone (SEZ) facilitation, support for the proposed Bihar Export Council, and export-readiness training programmes for MSMEs and producers. Learn More Highlights Adani Energy Solutions has won a transmission project in Bihar through Tariff Based Competitive Bidding The project will evacuate power from an upcoming 2,400 MW plant at Pirpainti It is expected to provide annual tariff of about ₹500 Crore once commissioned Delivery is targeted by the last quarter of 2028 through a dedicated SPV What the Company Announced Adani Energy Solutions Limited (NSE:ADANIENSOL) informed the stock exchanges on November 19, 2026 that it has won a transmission project for the evacuation of power from an upcoming 2,400 MW power plant in Pirpainti, Bihar. According to the company, the project was won through the Tariff Based Competitive Bidding (TBCB) mechanism and will provide annual tariff of about ₹500 Crore once commissioned. The project is titled “Evacuation of Power from 3X800 MW STPP Pirpainti”, which refers to three generating units of 800 MW each at a super thermal power plant. Project Structure and Timeline The company said the project will be implemented through a Special Purpose Vehicle (SPV), Vikramshila Power Transmission Ltd., and will be delivered by the last quarter of 2028. According to the media release, the project will evacuate power from Adani Power’s upcoming Pirpainti Ultra Super Critical Thermal Power Plant. Besides power evacuation, the company said the project will strengthen Bihar’s transmission network and enhance supply reliability. Scope of Work Adani Energy Solutions said the project comprises the construction of four Gas Insulated Substations (GIS) at Jhanjharpur, Bethauli and Begusarai, along with associated transformation capacity. The transmission infrastructure will include the 400 kV DCDS lines Pirpainti-Jhanjharpur, Pirpainti-Begusarai and Begusarai-Bakhtiyarpur, as well as the 220 kV DCDS lines Jhanjharpur-Bethauli and Begusarai-Begusarai Town. The work will also involve LILO (loop-in, loop-out) of existing 220 kV and 132 kV transmission lines at Jhanjharpur and the construction of 400 kV line bays at Bakhtiyarpur GSS. A LILO arrangement connects an existing line into a new substation so that power can flow in and out of it. Upon completion, the company said the project will add 881 circuit kilometres (ckm) of transmission lines and 3,160 MVA of transformation capacity to its portfolio. MVA (mega volt-ampere) indicates transformer capacity. Portfolio After the Win The company said the addition will take its transmission portfolio to 30,683 ckm and 146,585 MVA. With this project, Adani Energy Solutions said its transmission capital expenditure now stands at about ₹91,500 Crore. bihar_raw_news.title: Bihar's 'Nitish Setu' over Ganga set for inauguration - Awaz The Voice
bihar_raw_news.content: Bihar’s ‘Nitish Setu’ over Ganga set for inauguration Story by PTI | Posted by Vidushi Gaur | Date 20-11-2026 Prime Minister Narendra Modi Patna Prime Minister Narendra Modi will visit Bihar's Vaishali district on Saturday to inaugurate a Rs 5,500-crore bridge, named after former chief minister Nitish Kumar, over the Ganga, officials said. This would be the prime minister's first visit to the eastern state since May, when he had attended a function marking the expansion of the cabinet headed by Samrat Choudhary, the first BJP leader to lead a government in Bihar. The 9.76-km-long six-lane bridge, which connects Bidupur block in Vaishali to Kachchi Dargah on the outskirts of Patna, has been named 'Nitish Setu', in deference to the former chief minister, on whose watch the project was conceived, and came close to completion. Kumar, who heads the JD(U) and gave up the chief minister's post in April after a nearly two-decade-long tenure, had commissioned the project in 2012, though work began only in 2015, a year after the NDA government at the Centre helped the state borrow money from the Asian Development Bank (ADB), which has lent a total sum of Rs 3.472.15 crore. According to the state government, which has spent Rs 2,099.54 crore from its own resources on the project, the bridge, length of which nears 20 km if approach roads on both ends are taken into account, may turn a new leaf in the agrarian economy of densely populated north Bihar. The government expects, as a direct result of the bridge, much easier transportation of litchis, bananas, maize, vegetables and other agricultural produce from north Bihar, which is blessed with fertile soil but saddled with a dense population. The government is also confident that the 'Bidupur-Kachchi Dargah Corridor' will become an attractive destination for investors, as it had the potential of emerging as a hub of tourism and logistics. Besides, traffic congestion on the over 40-year-old Mahatma Gandhi Setu, connecting Patna and Hajipur, is expected to come down after 'Nitish Setu' becomes operational. Meanwhile, naming of the bridge has triggered a war of words between the ruling NDA and the main opposition party RJD, which has shared power with Nitish Kumar, albeit briefly, and seeks to claim its own share of credit. RJD working president Tejashwi Yadav, whose Raghopur assembly segment is set to benefit immensely from the bridge, has alleged that the BJP has sought to declare the JD(U) supremo as "politically dead", by naming the bridge after the leader while he was still alive. Yadav, who is now the leader of the opposition in the state assembly, has also claimed that in 2016, when he was the deputy CM with road construction as one of his portfolios, a proposal had been sent to Nitish Kumar for naming the bridge after Akshayvat Rai, a freedom fighter hailing from Bidupur. The project will also involve line-in-line-out arrangements for existing 220 kV and 132 kV lines at Jhanjharpur and construction of 400 kV line bays at Bakhtiyarpur grid substation. Upon completion, the project will add 881 ckm of transmission lines and 3,160 MVA of transformation capacity to AESL’s portfolio, taking it to 30,683 ckm and 146,585 MVA. Biology 💡 General Science - Physics 🧪 General Science - Chemistry 🗿 World History ✍️ Books & Authors 🔍 All GK Questions Categories Home Bihar Cabinet Approves Scholarship Hikes and Social Media Rules Bihar Cabinet Approves Scholarship Hikes and Social Media Rules On 29 January 2026, the Bihar Cabinet, chaired by Chief Minister Nitish Kumar, approved 31 proposals, including higher pre-matric scholarships for Other Backward Class (OBC) and Extremely Backward Class (EBC) students and amendments governing social media use by government employees. Higher Pre-Matric Scholarships Under the Mukhyamantri Pichchda Varg Evam Atyant Pichchda Varg Pre-Matric Chhatravritti Yojana, the Cabinet approved raising annual scholarships to ₹1,200 for Classes 1–4, ₹2,400 for Classes 5–6 and ₹3,600 for Classes 7–10. The Cabinet approved ₹1,751 crore for the scheme. Social Media Rules for Government Employees Amendments to the Bihar Government Servant Conduct Rules, 1976, were approved as the Bihar Government Servant Conduct (Amendment) Rules, 2026. Once the approved amendments are gazetted, employees would need prior permission from a competent authority before creating social media accounts and would be barred from using official IDs or numbers for personal accounts. The approved rules would prohibit objectionable comments, controversial posts and personal opinions on government policies or court orders. They would also restrict sharing classified information, making workplace-related videos and livestreaming official communications. Additional Chief Secretary (General Administration) B. bihar_raw_news.title: Away from Jharkhand, Bihar takes a development leap: Mega projects in focus ahead of PM ...
bihar_raw_news.content: Representational Pic Prime Minister Narendra Modi's proposed visit to Bihar on November 21 is bringing renewed attention to the state's infrastructure and development priorities.This is not the case with Jharkhand. With a major Ganga bridge set for inauguration, an industrial park planned in Vaishali and several strategic projects expected to gain momentum, the visit places connectivity, investment, employment and regional growth in focus.Jharkhand under the INDIA block led by the JMM- Congress- RJD is curiously watching or looking the other way as no major infrastructure development project worth its name of the Union government under the NDA rule led by the BJP and PM Modi, is in the pipeline. A BRIDGE THAT BRINGS TWO REGIONS CLOSER IN BIHAR The centrepiece of the visit will be the inauguration of the Kachchi Dargah–Bidupur six-lane Ganga bridge. Spanning 19.76 km, including a 9.76 km main bridge and 10 km of approach roads, the project has an estimated cost of around ₹5,700 crore. Connecting Patna with Vaishali, it is expected to reduce travel time between the two locations to approximately 20–25 minutes. It will also ease pressure on Mahatma Gandhi Setu, improve access to North Bihar and strengthen links with districts such as Samastipur, Darbhanga and Madhubani. INDUSTRIAL GROWTH AND EMPLOYMENT OPPORTUNITIES The second major development initiative is the proposed 1,234.42-acre industrial park and industrial corridor in Vaishali. Planned across five blocks, including Rajapakar, Jandaha, Mahua, Sahdei Buzurg and Raghopur, the project aims to attract investment, strengthen manufacturing and create employment opportunities. PROJECTS THAT COULD SHAPE BIHAR'S FUTURE The third development push centres on strategic projects, including the Patna–Purnia Expressway, a proposed Central University in Bhagalpur and a greenfield airport at Sultanganj. These projects are expected to receive further impetus, although their specific implementation milestones remain to be established. DEVELOPMENT MUST TRANSLATE INTO OPPORTUNITY With the NDA government completing its first year in Bihar on November 20, the Prime Minister's visit the following day carries added significance. The real measure of development, however, will be how effectively infrastructure translates into jobs, accessible services, stronger businesses and better opportunities across the state. bihar_raw_news.title: Matter of pride for Bihar : JD(U)'s Sanjay Jha welcomes bridge named after Nitish Kumar
bihar_raw_news.content: Matter of pride for Bihar: JD(U)'s Sanjay Jha welcomes bridge named after Nitish Kumar ANI | Updated: Nov 20, 2026 10:36 IST ANI News Join our Whatsapp channel Patna ( Bihar ) [ India ], November 20 (ANI): Janata Dal (United) working president Sanjay Jha on Friday said the inauguration of a bridge, Nitish Setu, named after Bihar Chief Minister Nitish Kumar by Prime Minister Narendra Modi, would be a matter of pride for the people of the state, adding that the project would significantly improve connectivity between North and South Bihar . Nitish Setu is the new name for the six-lane bridge over the Ganga River connecting Kacchi Dargah–Bidupur in Bihar . Speaking to the reporters, Jha said, "The Prime Minister is coming to Bihar tomorrow, and it is a matter of great happiness. He will inaugurate a bridge that has been named after our leader, Nitish Kumar. I believe this will provide major connectivity between South Bihar and North Bihar . It will make a significant difference to economic activity, trade and the movement of people." He said former Chief Minister Nitish Kumar's contributions over the past 20 years, particularly in infrastructure development, deserved recognition. Recalling the difficulties faced by people in flood-prone areas of North Bihar , Jha said the construction of bridges had made travel easier for residents of Sitamarhi , Madhubani and Darbhanga . He added that the people of Bihar would be happy to see the Chief Minister's work being recognised through the naming of the bridge. "This is not about Nitish ji's prestige. The people of Bihar feel that he deserves this recognition. They feel happy when something is named after him, as it allows people to remember his work. The fact that the Prime Minister himself is inaugurating the project is an additional reason for happiness," Jha said. Responding to Congress leader Rahul Gandhi's remarks that the country was facing an economic crisis and the media was ignoring it, Jha said Gandhi spoke negatively about the country and rarely acknowledged its achievements. He referred to the COVID-19 pandemic and the ongoing global tensions involving Iran and the United States, saying the Centre had managed the impact of the crises and ensured that the situation did not get out of control. "Rahul Gandhi ji never says anything positive about the country apart from speaking negatively. Have you ever heard him say something good? There was such a big COVID crisis. Did the country recover from it or not? At what level was the economy growing?" he said. Jha further added that global conflicts, including the war in Ukraine and tensions involving Iran, affected economies across the world, including India . He also said India was the world's fifth-largest economy and that development projects were continuing despite global challenges. His remarks came after Rahul Gandhi, speaking at Columbia University in the United States on Wednesday, said India was heading towards a looming economic crisis, citing unemployment and concerns over the country's education system. national_raw_news.title: 57th International Film Festival of India to begin today in Goa with grand opening ceremony
national_raw_news.content: The 57th edition of the International Film Festival of India, IFFI 2026, begins today with a grand opening ceremony in the evening. Chief Minister Pramod Sawant and festival director, filmmaker Ashutosh Gowariker will be inaugurating the nine-day cinematic extravaganza that would see cinema lovers, filmmakers, artists and actors coming together to celebrate the magic of cinema. The theme for this year’s edition, ‘Stories Without Borders’, befits the spirit of the festival that will see an array of cinematic stories converge on the shores of Goa. The opening Film ‘Fatherland’ directed by Pawel Pawlikoski will be screened today across all the venues of the festival. Akashvani correspondents reported that Goa is decked up with vibrant lights and decorations, in line with the theme of the festival, ‘Stories Without Borders’. Featuring over 150 international films from 86 countries, IFFI 2026 promises a diverse cinematic experience, showcasing compelling narratives, emerging talent and acclaimed filmmakers. The festival will also provide a platform for meaningful conversations, masterclasses, industry interactions and discussions on the evolving landscape of world cinema. Among the major highlights are the opening film, Fatherland, by Polish filmmaker Paweł Pawlikowski, and the closing film, We Are All Strangers, by Singaporean filmmaker Anthony Chen. With special sections on animation and films about filmmaking, alongside masterclasses, workshops, competitions and the WAVES Film Bazaar, IFFI 2026 aims to strengthen India’s engagement with the global film industry while celebrating the diversity and transformative power of cinema. IFFI 2026 promises to be not just a celebration of films but also a meeting ground for cultures, creative ideas and stories that transcend geographical and linguistic boundaries.

national_raw_news.content: The Indian women’s hockey team defeated Malaysia 4-1 in the Women’s Asian Hockey Champions Trophy being held in Bhopal, Madhya Pradesh. Khan Mumtaz, captain Salima Tete, Pooja Sahu and Lalremsiami scored one goal each for India. Nuramirah Zulkifli scored the only goal for Malaysia. Earlier in the day, China defeated Thailand 7-0 in the opening match. Feng Qiagmiao and Deng Qiuchan scored two goals each for China, while three other players scored one goal each. In the second match of the day, Japan defeated South Korea 1-0. The match remained goalless until the final minutes. In the 59th minute, Saito Hanami scored from a penalty corner to give Japan the win. Chief Minister Dr. Mohan Yadav inaugurated the tournament today. The stadium was lit up with a grand fireworks display, and a large number of spectators came to watch the matches. Six countries, including India, are taking part in the tournament. The tournament is being held at the International Sports Complex in Barkheda Nathu, Bhopal, from November 19 to 28. Entry to the stadium is free for spectators. On Saturday, China will play Malaysia at 2:30 PM, Thailand will face Japan at 4:45 PM, and hosts India will take on South Korea at 7 PM.

national_raw_news.title: Union Minister Piyush Goyal urges Indian businesses to utilise opportunities opened by recent FTAs 4 hours ago 49
national_raw_news.content: Union Commerce and Industry Minister Piyush Goyal has urged Indian businesses to utilise opportunities opened by recent free trade agreements(FTAs). Addressing the valedictory session of FICCI’s Annual General Meeting and Annual Convention in New Delhi yesterday, Mr Goyal said, India’s preferential access to global markets has expanded by an additional 60 trillion dollars over the last four-and-a-half years, taking the total to approximately 70 trillion dollars. Referring to his recent visits to Egypt and Italy, the Minister said that the growing interest of international partners in working with India reflects the country’s increasing global standing. He noted that discussions have been initiated to explore a Preferential Trade Agreement or Free Trade Agreement with Egypt, while the forthcoming India-EU FTA has generated considerable interest among Italian businesses. He said that the commitment of international businesses to work with India reflects the growing opportunities for trade, investment and industrial cooperation. Highlighting the country’s growing economic strength and global engagement, Mr Goyal said that India has set a target of achieving 1 trillion dollars in exports in Financial Year 2026-27. He noted that the country recorded exports of 480 billion dollars in the first six months of the current financial year. The Minister spoke about India’s transformation over the past decade, noting improvements in infrastructure, digital connectivity, financial inclusion and the banking sector. He added that the country’s growing middle class, purchasing power and expanding domestic market provide a strong foundation for economic growth.

national_raw_news.title: UP govt decides to allocate 4.19 acres of govt land in Varanasi to strengthen security arrangements at Shri Kashi Vishwanath Dham 2 hours ago 41
national_raw_news.content: The Uttar Pradesh government has decided to allocate 4.19 acres of government land in Varanasi, on lease to the Union Ministry of Home Affairs, to strengthen security arrangements at the Shri Kashi Vishwanath Dham. The decision aims to facilitate the permanent deployment of Central Armed Police Forces near the temple complex and ensure a swift response in emergency situations. The allocation will, however, remain subject to the final decision of the competent court. The land, measuring 1.697 hectares, is located in the Sadar tehsil of Varanasi, in villages Kila Kohna and Saretabad. According to the prevailing circle rate, its estimated market value is around 44.04 crore rupees. The land will be allotted free of cost for a maximum period of 90 years, through successive renewals of 30 years each, under the special provisions of the Government Property Management (Amendment) Rules, 2003. Following the redevelopment of the Kashi Vishwanath Dham, lakhs of devotees, tourists and distinguished visitors from India and abroad visit the temple every day. Considering the growing footfall and the sensitive nature of the area, the permanent deployment of central security forces is expected to further strengthen its multi-layered security arrangements. Under the terms of the lease, the land will remain non-transferable and can be used exclusively for the designated purpose of strengthening security. Ownership of the land will continue to vest with the Revenue Department of the Uttar Pradesh government. The lease deed will be executed by the District Magistrate of Varanasi on behalf of the Governor of Uttar Pradesh.

national_raw_news.title: India records $11.3 bn FPIs in first 18 days of November: CEA Anantha Nageswaran
national_raw_news.content: Chief Economic Adviser, Dr. V. Anantha Nageswaran today said that foreign capital is returning sharply to India as oil prices cool below 100 dollars per barrel and the emerging risks regarding AI valuation. Addressing the 65th General Assembly and Annual Meeting of the World Federation of Exchanges (WFE) in Mumbai, Dr. Nageswaran said India has recorded foreign portfolio inflows of 11.3 billion dollars in just the first 18 days of November. The CEA further underlined that India remains poised to be a big beneficiary in the course of the next financial year as the AI bubble comes down to realistic levels, adding that earlier currency pressures from AI outflows will now likely turn into a source of currency strength. He also highlighted that India has sustained roughly 7 per cent real GDP growth despite global tariff turmoil, supply shocks, and geopolitical conflicts, adding that India has been successful in lifting roughly 500 million people above the 4.20 dollar-a-day moderate poverty line, with rural poverty falling faster than urban in the past decade. While noting that the Indian Government, which had been cautious about trade liberalisation until around 2020, Dr. Nageswaran said that the government has embraced free trade agreements with considerable enthusiasm in the post-pandemic period. He said that India has not only concluded but also operationalised trade agreements with the UK, Oman and New Zealand this year alone. He added that a trade agreement with the European Union has also been concluded while trade agreements with the US and Canada are also imminent. Pointing towards India’s strong export performance in the current financial year, the CEA said exports of goods and services stood at around 569 billion dollars from April to October, registering a growth of nearly 17 percent. Talking about the goal of Viksit Bharat by 2047, the CEA flagged five unique challenges – geopolitical fragmentation, China’s manufacturing scale, the energy trilemma, AI-led job shifts, and social media’s impact on youth cognitive skills. To counter these, the CEA said closing technology gaps will buy resilience for India, while agriculture, trade skills, and human-centric services will buy leverage for India.

Top Stories of the Day Share DD India November 20, 2026 8:22 AM IST Prime Minister | SCO | Shanghai Cooperation Organisation | SCO Civilisational Dialogue Forum | Narendra Modi | PM Modi PM Modi to inaugurate first SCO Civilisational Dialogue Forum in New Delhi on November 20 Author: DD India Prime Minister Narendra Modi will inaugurate the first Shanghai Cooperation Organisation (SCO) Civilisational Dialogue Forum at Purana Qila in New Delhi on November 20, at around 5:30 PM. He will also address the gathering on the occasion. The three-day Forum, scheduled from November 20 to 22, aims to celebrate the rich and interconnected civilisational heritage of SCO member countries, strengthen people-to-people ties and promote cross-cultural dialogue and cooperation. The initiative follows a proposal made by PM Modi at the SCO Summit in Tianjin, China, in 2025 to establish a dedicated platform for civilisational dialogue under the SCO framework. The proposal was subsequently welcomed in the Bishkek Declaration of the organisation. Cultural showcase to highlight India-Eurasia connections The inaugural ceremony will feature a cultural presentation titled “Civilisations in Conversation – Cultural Show”, combining music, dance, visual storytelling and narration. Based on the theme “Vasudhaiva Kutumbakam – The World Is One Family”, the presentation will highlight cultural connections between India and the wider Eurasian region. The Forum will also host exhibitions showcasing India’s archaeological, artistic and literary heritage under the title “ASTITVA – The Essence of Our Existence.” The exhibition will offer visitors an immersive account of Delhi’s history through archaeological evidence dating from 1200 BCE to 1200 CE. It will include excavated remains, artefacts, architectural fragments and other significant discoveries. Another key attraction will be the “Mahabharat Scroll Pavilion – Anant: A Rare 18th Century Mahabharata Scroll”, featuring an illustrated scroll that reflects India’s rich epic and artistic traditions. Four thematic sessions to explore shared civilisational heritage Four thematic sessions will be organised on November 21 and 22, bringing together scholars, academics, subject experts and cultural representatives from across the SCO region. The discussions will explore a range of shared cultural and intellectual traditions, including music and performing arts, textiles, cuisine and traditional games. Participants will also examine common traditions in art and architecture, as well as language and literary heritage, including scripts and manuscripts. Monastic trails and philosophical traditions will form another key area of discussion. national_raw_news.content: Srinagar to get Rs 361 cr waste processing facility at Achan Advertisment Breaking News Top Stories Srinagar to get Rs 361 cr waste processing facility at Achan RK News 20 Nov 2026 03:32 IST Follow Us 125-tonne construction waste plant targeted for Dec 91,789 tonnes of accumulated material processed at dumpsite Srinagar, Nov 19: In a major move to strengthen solid waste management in Srinagar, the Srinagar Municipal Corporation (SMC) has proposed an integrated waste processing facility with a capacity of 800 tonnes per day at Achan, involving an estimated investment of Rs 361 crore, while 91,789 tonnes of accumulated waste have already been processed at the dumpsite as part of efforts to reclaim the site and reduce environmental risks. Joint Commissioner, Srinagar Municipal Corporation, Syed Abul Qasim, disclosed these details during a press briefing organised by the Press Information Bureau (PIB), Jammu, in collaboration with the Jammu and Kashmir Pollution Control Committee (JKPCC) on Thursday to discuss the implementation of the Solid Waste Management Rules, 2026. Qasim said the proposed facility at Achan would include multiple waste processing components aimed at reducing dependence on conventional dumping and improving the recovery of reusable materials. The project, estimated to cost Rs 361 crore, will have facilities for material recovery, compressed biogas generation, composting and refuse-derived fuel processing. He said the integrated facility would enable the processing of different categories of municipal waste and support efforts to recover useful resources from waste generated across Srinagar. Highlighting the ongoing work at the Achan dumpsite near Anchar Lake, Qasim said approximately 91,789 tonnes of waste had already been processed as part of measures to reclaim the site and address environmental concerns associated with accumulated waste. The processing work, he said, is aimed at recovering useful materials, reducing the volume of accumulated waste and limiting environmental risks at the site. The Joint Commissioner also informed that a leachate treatment plant has been proposed at Achan to address environmental concerns arising from liquid waste generated at the dumping site. Leachate, the contaminated liquid that forms when water passes through accumulated waste, requires treatment to prevent potential pollution of surrounding soil and water resources. In another development, Qasim said a construction and demolition waste processing plant with a capacity of 125 tonnes per day is projected to be completed by December 2026. The facility is intended to strengthen the city's capacity to process waste generated from construction and demolition activities rather than allowing such material to accumulate at dumping locations. The proposed projects form part of SMC's efforts to improve waste processing infrastructure and address longstanding waste management challenges in the city. Meanwhile, Chairman JKPCC, Vasu Yadav, said the Solid Waste Management Rules, 2026, introduce stricter provisions for waste segregation, scientific processing and accountability among waste generators. He said the new framework requires segregation of waste at source into four categories — wet waste, dry waste, sanitary waste and special care waste. The Press Information Bureau (PIB), Jammu, in collaboration with JKPCC, organised a press briefing to explain the key provisions of the new Rules and sensitise media organisations and the public about the responsibilities of different stakeholders. The Rules place particular emphasis on segregation of waste at source into four categories—wet, dry, sanitary and special care waste. The framework also seeks to strengthen scientific waste processing, recycling, resource recovery and remediation of legacy dumpsites, while ensuring greater accountability among waste generators. JKPCC Chairman Vasu Yadav said the Rules provide for measures such as user fees, spot fines and environmental compensation to ensure compliance. He stressed that effective implementation would require coordinated action by government agencies, institutions, commercial establishments and citizens. Yadav said source segregation and scientific processing must become an integral part of waste management practices, adding that recycling and resource recovery were important for reducing the burden on disposal sites. In her opening remarks, Director PIB Jammu Neha Jalali said the press briefing was organised to familiarise media organisations and the public with the provisions of the Rules and promote awareness about responsible waste disposal. She said effective implementation would require behavioural change and active participation of citizens, institutions and local authorities. Jalali also highlighted the role of the media in disseminating information, encouraging source segregation and taking the message of cleanliness and sustainable waste management to the grassroots to achieve the objectives of Swachh Bharat. Commissioner Jammu Municipal Corporation Ayushi Sudan highlighted the Corporation’s initiatives to strengthen waste management and improve accountability among bulk waste generators.
